changes.text: V.I.P. uses Field 62.20 - Merchant Verification Value (MVV) to identify and authenticate merchants in authorization and reversal requests. It also validates the relationship between the merchant and its Visa client. Acquirers and issuers must successfully complete testing to send and receive this field. To be able to send and receive field 62.20, acquirers and issuers must be able to send field 62 in bitmap format. Visa assigns MVVs to specific merchants, and each MVV is unique. Visa assigns the first six positions and helps the acquirer assign the last four. If the MVV field format is invalid in requests, V.I.P. drops the field. U.S. tax payment transactions must include an MVV. MVVs can also be used to allow individual clients to process transactions while belonging to an otherwise blocked merchant category such as 7995 (online gambling).

path: Summary of V.I.P. Full Service Processing Services and Capabilities
changes.text: V.I.P. uses Field 62.20—Merchant Verification Value (MVV) to identify and authenticate merchants in authorization and reversal requests. It also validates the relationship between the merchant and its Visa client. V.I.P. uses a Merchant Verification Value (MVV) to identify merchants and track the volume of transactions processed by individual global merchants. V.I.P. also uses the MVV ID for transaction processing such as online gambling, merchant risk scoring, and other services based on MVV ID flags. Visa assigns MVVs to specific merchants, and each MVV is unique. Visa assigns the first six positions and helps the acquirer assign the last four. If the MVV field format is invalid in requests, V.I.P. drops the field. The MVV is not necessarily a component of the Custom Payment Service. U.S. tax payment transactions must include an MVV. MVVs can also be used to allow individual clients to process transactions while belonging to an otherwise blocked merchant category such as 7995 (online gambling). MVVs are stored in the cardholder database (CDB) and are maintained by the client. Acquirers must provide the MVV in all authorization, clearing, and exception item messages if the merchant has an MVV assigned. Issuers must retain and return the MVV in all exception items. To be able to send and receive field 62.20, acquirers and issuers must be able to send field 62 in bitmap format. Acquirers and issuers must successfully complete testing to send and receive this field.

text_a: The Visa Token Service provides clients enhanced protection against counterfeit, account misuse, and other forms of fraud in card-not-present and hybrid transaction environments. This service helps to minimize unauthorized use of cardholder account data in a transaction. The Visa Token Service uses the EMV Payment Tokenization Specification–Technical Framework (payment token framework) published by EMVCo addressing processing considerations and use of payment tokens to protect cardholder payment credentials. Visa Token Service allows acquirers, merchants, and digital wallet providers to request for tokens. Tokens are surrogate values which replace the PAN in transaction processing. Token vaults generate and store tokens along with their associated PANs and issue them when requested. Token service providers operate token vaults. Token requestors can request tokens at different stages of the transaction including authorization, capture, clearing, and exception processing. The PAN is never passed in the transaction when a token is requested, this enhances the security during transaction processing.

path: Full Service POS Products for Issuers
text_a: Participating issuers can process Visa POS and Interlink transactions using one message format and one connection to the V.I.P. system. They can also use the same connection to support their full service ATM services. Full service POS issuers can immediately authorize and post online financial transactions received from full service POS acquirers. In addition, Visa POS issuers must have the ability to authorize transactions online and to receive online deferred clearing transactions through V.I.P. at a later time. For batch-deferred clearing transactions from authorization-only/BASE II Visa POS acquirers or for online-deferred clearing transactions from full service acquirers, issuers receive the authorization message at the time of purchase and the clearing message later. VisaNet delivers the authorization and clearing messages through the issuer's full service VisaNet connection, enabling the issuer to maintain one consistent method for processing all Visa-branded products. The main function of issuers' systems is to accurately respond, based on cardholders' accounts and PINs, to messages received from the V.I.P. System. Issuers also must send dispute financials, administrative messages, and network management messages. Issuers receive transaction requests and approve or decline them based on predefined parameters. section_new_paragraphs: Creating an Advice Under normal conditions, when STIP responds to an authorization or a financial transaction, it creates an advice for the issuer (unless the issuer participates in the Preauthorization Stand-In Service). Advice message types are:
0120 for an 0100 request 0220 for an 0200 request

A STIP advice contains all of the data from the acquirer's request, except the PIN, security- related control information, and track data. In addition to the data from the acquirer's request, a STIP advice contains:

The STIP response code (in Field 39-Response Code). The reason STIP processed the request (in Subfield 63.4-STIP/Switch Reason Code). Code 1 in the Advices-Created-By flag in the message header. (This code indicates that STIP created the advice while standing in for the issuer.) Settlement flags in the message header of the advice. (STIP sets these flags as needed to indicate the settlement impact.) For more information, see the Message Structure and Header Field Specifications chapter of the pertinent V.I.P. System technical specifications manuals.
Advices remain on file until the issuer signs on to Advice Recovery mode using an 0800 network management message. STIP does not create advices for:
Account transfer Product eligibility inquiry Balance inquiry

V.I.P. ensures a response code 57 (declined) is always returned for a recurring or installment payments purchase, product eligibility or account verification message, occurring on a non- reloadable prepaid card and create a 0120 or 0220 advice for the issuer. Creating a Reversal Advice When STIP responds to a reversal, it creates an 0420 advice for the issuer to recover. V.I.P. stores advices online for 30 days. Issuers that want to retrieve their advices need to retrieve them within this 30-day period. The 0420 advice contains data from the undeliverable reversal and the STIP response. The Advice-Created-By flag of the 0420 message header contains code 1, indicating that STIP created the advice while standing in for the issuer. STIP also sets the settlement flags in the message header of the advice as needed, to indicate the settlement impact. In addition, the 0420 advice contains a reason code in Subfield 63.4-STIP/Switch Reason Code.
